title: Growth Surge Playbook: Private VPC + SLA Bundle (QBR Template + Renewal Tracker)
content:
Executive summary:
This doc is a compact, deployable QBR + renewal tracker + outreach playbook specifically designed to convert production users to (a) Dedicated reserved capacity, (b) Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, and (c) premium SLA bundles. It is intentionally tactical: slide-by-slide QBR prompts, a lightweight renewal tracker, a risk-indexed upsell framework, technical prerequisites checklist, pricing bundle examples, outreach templates, and an implementation timeline with measurable KPIs.

Why this is different (and targeted):
- Focus on high-signal indicators that predict willingness to commit (latency variability, token spend concentration, KV cache hit patterns, regional isolation needs).
- Risk-indexed ask sizing: tie recommended offers to reliability and compliance risk to justify premium SLAs and private deployments.
- Low-friction commercial packaging + engineering readiness checklist to speed proof-of-value.

QBR slide deck outline (15–20 minutes for execs + 30–40 minutes for technical deep-dive):
1) Title / Attendees / Objective (1 slide): frame the QBR as a decision conversation (retain, optimize, commit).
2) Snapshot: current usage & health (2 slides)
   - 90/30/7 day token burn, p50/p95 latency, error categories (and % impact on calls)
   - Concentration: top 5 routes by cost, top 3 customers/tenants by spend (anonymized)
3) Reliability risk map (2 slides)
   - SLA gaps vs observed incidents, regional failover gaps, warm-start cold-start frequency
4) Economics: unit cost and delta to Dedicated/Private (2 slides)
   - Measured current cost per 1k tokens, projected cost after batching/quantization, and committed pricing examples
5) Migration/Onramp options (2 slides)
   - Canary -> phased shift -> dedicated standing pool -> private deployment timeline
6) Proposed offer(s) (2 slides)
   - Tiered bundle: Dedicated-lite (reserved baseline + burst), Private-VPC starter, Premium SLA (99.9/99.95/penalty tiers)
7) Technical readiness checklist (1 slide)
8) ROI example & success metrics (1 slide)
9) Ask & next steps (1 slide)

Renewal / Opportunity tracker (CSV columns for quick copy-paste):
- Account ID, Account Name, ARR (current), 90D token spend, Top routes, Current plan, Suggested upgrade, Suggested commit (USD/mo), Priority score (1-10), Exec sponsor, SE owner, Renewal date, Next touch, Status (open/in_contract/closed-won/closed-lost), Notes

Priority scoring (one-line heuristic to triage accounts):
- Score = min(10, round( 0.4*token_concentration_score + 0.3*latency_risk_score + 0.2*compliance_need + 0.1*exec_sponsor_availability ))
- token_concentration_score: how much of account traffic routes through a small number of models/routes (0-10).
- latency_risk_score: p95/p50 delta and SLO miss frequency (0-10).
- compliance_need: 0/5/10 (none / needs VPC / needs on-prem).
- exec_sponsor_availability: 0/5/10 (no sponsor / champion / exec sponsor)

Risk-indexed uplift framework (short):
- Low risk (score 0–3): propose Dedicated-lite commit. Low friction; focus on cost per token and burst headroom.
- Medium risk (4–7): propose Dedicated + optional 1-region VPC, 6–12 month commit, include a 30-day private-preview migration slot.
- High risk (8–10): propose Private deployment + premium SLA, start with a 90-day private pilot, include KMS/HSM integration and SOC2 audit readiness support.

Pricing bundle samples (illustrative, local currency/discounts vary per account):
- Dedicated-lite: baseline 2 x A100-equivalent pool, reserved throughput, 20% discount off on-demand, burst capacity priced at 1.5x baseline unit. Suggested commit: $12k–$35k/mo.
- Private-VPC Starter: includes control plane access from Redwood, customer-managed network, 99.9% SLA. Setup fee + monthly platform charge; suggested commit: $25k–$75k/mo.
- Premium SLA bundle: 99.95% SLA, 30-minute escalation, dedicated TAM, additional observability retention. Premium: +15–30% over Private-VPC Starter.

Technical prerequisites checklist (copyable for engagement kickoff):
- Network: IP allowlist and peering tested, egress/inbound rules validated.
- Identity: SSO/SAML + SCIM or service principal created.
- Secrets: KMS/HSM integration plan, rotation schedule.
- Data residency: mapping of data flows and storage targets.
- Model artifacts: model version pinning, quantization artifacts, and weights availability.
- Observability: sample traces exported, route-level latency breakdown, token-level billing exported to customer BI.

Migration / Onramp play (3-phased):
Phase A (2–4 weeks): baseline telemetry + economics analysis + canary route on Dedicated-lite. Goal: prove cost and latency profile.
Phase B (4–8 weeks): migrate 30–60% traffic; validate KV cache behavior and throughput. Provide runbook for rollback and fallback to hosted API.
Phase C (4–12 weeks): full cutover to Private or Dedicated baseline. SLA activation and runbook handoff to SRE/TAM.

Customer-facing outreach cadence (8 weeks):
- Week 0: Executive QBR invite + one-pager (value + ask)
- Week 1: Technical readiness sync (SE-led)
- Week 2: Economics deep-dive (finance + product)
- Week 3: Pilot kickoff + telemetry baseline
- Week 6: Pilot review + recommended commit
- Week 8: Final negotiation / contract signature

Short email templates (editable):
- Executive invite: "Wanted to block 30 minutes for a QBR focused on reliability and economics — we have a recommended pathway that could reduce unit cost by ~X% and give you a dedicated SLA. Can we meet next week?"
- SE follow-up: "Thanks for the time — attaching the technical checklist and a short plan for a canary. If you can confirm network peering windows we’ll schedule infra prep."

Objection handling cheatsheet (snippets):
- "We can’t justify cost": show 90-day burn + per-call unit economics and model how batching/quantization will reduce marginal spend; show break-even timeline.
- "We’re not ready for private": propose a Private Preview (90 days) or hybrid where only high-sensitivity routes are isolated.
- "SLA too expensive": decompose SLA into response & resolution targets and recommend a middle-ground 99.9% with escalation credits.

Success metrics / KPIs for the program (report weekly during pilot):
- p95 latency trend (target: < baseline + 10%)
- Token unit cost delta (target: reduce by 10–25% within 60 days)
- Cache hit ratio for KV/prefix (target: >70% for conversational workloads)
- Incidents impacting customer routes (target: zero P1 within contract period)
- Time to targeted throughput for migrated routes (target: < 14 days)

Implementation timeline (sample 12-week calendar):
- Week 0–2: QBR + contract framing
- Week 2–4: Network + identity + infra prechecks
- Week 4–8: Pilot (canary + telemetry)
- Week 8–10: Review + commit decision
- Week 10–12: Cutover + SLA handover

Appendix A — quick migration cost-delta calculator (text formula you can drop in spreadsheet):
- Current_monthly_cost = sum_over_routes( avg_tokens_per_call * calls_per_day * 30 * cost_per_1k_tokens )
- Dedicated_estimate = baseline_reservation_cost + (projected_burst_tokens/1000 * reserved_rate)
- Delta = Current_monthly_cost - Dedicated_estimate (positive -> savings)
- Include sensitivity lines for p50/p95 token sizes and cache hit improvements (+/- 10/20/30%)

Appendix B — quick checklist for legal/commercial (for GTM handoff):
- Confirmation of data residency & export controls
- IP/OSS use cases for hosted model artifacts
- SLAs spelled with credits and operational definitions
- Term & termination clauses for pilot vs committed plans

Next steps (for internal team):
1) Owner: Maya Chen — schedule internal sync with Finance and PM to validate sample pricing ranges.
2) SEs: Diego to run 3 account econ analyses using the Delta calculator by EOD next Friday.
3) Legal: Sana to draft a 90-day Private Preview T&Cs template.
4) Close loop: Tom to prep QBR slide skeleton and share with account owners.

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- Should we automate the Priority score calculation in Console for top X accounts? (worth Engineering effort if > 50 accounts flagged).
- Explore a self-serve Private-VPC trial (1 node) for strategic early customers — ops cost analysis needed.
- Need a one-page legal appendix for EU data residency check that maps to Private vs Dedicated differences.

End of playbook (working draft).
